$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

architect.rationale: single-loop with five ordered commits on one branch of the orchestra git repo. Not a diamond: the slices cannot be given disjoint file sets. src-tauri/src/session/mod.rs is the hub every backend feature changes (s1 publish/events_for, s2 Spawner signature and resume path, s3 on_output transcript hook and new Event variant, s5 notifier after publish); lib.rs is touched by s3 (transcript dir, event channel, command) and s5 (plugin, notifier); commands.rs by s2 and s3; types.ts/ipc.ts by s2 and s4; state.ts by s1 and s4. Separate branches would guarantee a fan-in conflict in mod.rs. Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock appear only in s5. s1 goes first because it restructures publish/events_for, which s3 extends with per-line work; s4 goes last because it consumes the settings types from s2 and the IPC from s3. Risk tags: every slice touches a file another slice also touches (mod.rs, or types.ts/ipc.ts/state.ts), which is high by the fleet rule. In addition, s2 decides which flags reach the claude command line and whether the inbox gate can be bypassed; s3 writes tool output (which can contain secrets from the user project) to disk and derives a file path from a session id; s5 adds a native plugin dependency and a hook beside the locks. s4 is high only by the shared-file rule. It has no sensitive data, so its reviewer can focus on merge-by-seq and canPrompt.

plan.intent: D2 follow-up (1) (gate G1): stop cloning the whole inbox and the whole snapshot on every stdout line. (a) SessionState gets a non-persisted inbox_rev counter, bumped on every inbox mutation. Session keeps the last emitted rev, and events_for emits InboxUpdated only when the rev changed, carrying only the items of that session. (b) A snapshot is queued only when status, inbox_rev or claude_session_id changed, or from an explicit command (start, answer, reply, stop, add_project). Text-only lines (last_message, last_activity_at) mark the session dirty and are saved by the next significant save or by shutdown, which always snapshots. (c) Frontend reducer: inbox-updated upserts by id (the event copy wins) and never drops items of other sessions; inbox-loaded keeps mergeInbox.

plan.intent: Transcript backend, kept out of SessionState, PersistedSession and state.json. New session/transcript.rs with a pure entries_from_value(&Value) -> Vec<Entry>. Entry kinds: UserPrompt{text} (recorded by Orchestra on start, reply and resume), AssistantText{text}, ToolUse{id,name,input_preview}, ToolResult{tool_use_id,is_error,content}, TurnResult{is_error,subtype,total_cost_usd,duration_ms,num_turns,usage{input,output,cache_read,cache_creation}}, and Truncated. tool_result content accepts a string or an array of blocks: text blocks are joined, image/base64 blocks become the placeholder [image], unknown blocks become [block type]. Caps: 8 KiB per text or content field and 2 KiB for tool input JSON, truncated on a char boundary with a truncated flag. Per-session file cap is 16 MiB; past it, one Truncated entry is written and appends stop. A TranscriptStore owned by Sessions has a Disk(app_data_dir/transcripts) or Memory backend (Memory for tests, or when storage is off). The file name comes only from an id that is s followed by digits and exists in the session map. Each session gets one append-only JSONL file, appended synchronously from its reader thread under a per-session mutex that is never held together with Inner. Each entry gets a seq, lazily initialised from the file on first touch. on_output parses the line once, computes entries before taking Inner, appends them, and passes them to publish as Event::TranscriptAppended{session_id, entries}. lib.rs emits that as transcript-appended. A new command get_transcript{session_id} (deny_unknown_fields) returns the last 1000 entries plus next_seq. protocol.rs exposes a parse-from-Value entry so each line is parsed once. Cost is never summed: the latest TurnResult is the session total as reported by claude.

plan.intent: OS notifications. New src-tauri/src/notify.rs with a pure decide(before: SessionStatus, after: SessionStatus, new_item: Option<InboxKind>) -> Option<Notice> where Notice.kind is one of NeedsInput, Finished, Errored, Failed. It fires on entering WaitingPermission/WaitingQuestion/NeedsAttention from a non-waiting status, on entering Idle with a new Finished or Error item, and on entering Failed. It never fires on waiting->waiting, on Stop (Ended), on Suspended, or on Starting->Working. Sessions takes a Notify callback; on_output records the status before apply and calls decide after publish, outside Inner and emit_order. Restore never calls apply, and shutdown makes on_output return early, so neither one notifies. lib.rs registers tauri-plugin-notification 2.6.x and implements the callback: it skips when is_focused() on the main window is Ok(true), otherwise it calls app.notification().builder() with title Orchestra and body <project>: needs your input / finished / turn failed / session failed, then show(). The callback never calls Sessions. No capability is added, because the plugin is called from Rust only, as dialog is. The body carries the project name and the kind only: no prompt, question or result text.

plan.intent: Session detail view and follow-up prompts. The reducer gains a selected session id. Clicking a session card opens SessionDetail in place of the Inbox column, and Back returns. The detail header shows status, project, model and mode. A cost block shows the latest TurnResult, labelled session total reported by claude, plus last-turn tokens. The transcript list subscribes to transcript-appended first, then calls get_transcript and merges by seq, so nothing is lost or duplicated. Text renders as React text only: no markdown and no dangerouslySetInnerHTML; long fields are collapsed. The prompt box is enabled for Idle (whether the last item is Finished or Error) and for Suspended (which goes through the existing reply and the D2 lazy resume). It is disabled, with a visible reason, for Starting/Working/Waiting*/NeedsAttention, and absent for Ended/Failed. It sends answer with kind reply as today, and the Rust refusal remains the authority. Strict decoders for the new event and command drop malformed payloads.

gate_decisions: G1: include the D2 follow-up (1) fix as slice s1 of D3, before any per-line transcript work. Recommended: yes.
G2: transcript persistence. Recommended: persist as append-only JSONL per session under app_data_dir/transcripts (s3 as written).

G3: permission-mode allowlist. Recommended: manual, acceptEdits, plan, plus Default = no flag. This CLI (2.1.296) does NOT accept default: its choices are acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, manual, dontAsk and plan, so the suggested default becomes manual. acceptEdits by design lets file edits through without an inbox item, and the UI labels it so. Pre-merge human-read probe P1 (one-off, outside the repo, a few API turns): run claude -p with --permission-prompt-tool stdio under each of manual, acceptEdits and plan, ask for a Bash write, and confirm a can_use_tool control_request arrives. Any mode that does not emit it is removed before merge.

G4: model allowlist opus, sonnet, fable (the three aliases in claude --help) plus Default = no flag. Validated as a Rust enum on the IPC struct (serde rejects anything else) and again on load. haiku stays out until a live probe shows the alias is accepted.

G5: schema stays at 1. Settings are serde(default) Option<String> fields on StoredSession, parsed through the allowlist on load (unknown -> None). Reason: the D2 build has no deny_unknown_fields, so it loads a D3 file and ignores the fields. Storing strings rather than a serde enum on disk means a future variant can never make the whole load of an older build Unreadable (store.rs:87). Accepted cost: if the owner downgrades to D2 and that build saves, the settings are dropped and those sessions resume with no flags.

G6: cost is shown as the latest total_cost_usd, labelled session total reported by claude, and never summed. Whether it resets in a --resume process is unknown; if it does, the reset will show in the UI rather than be hidden.
G7: the notification body carries the project name and kind only (no question, prompt or result text), because toasts show on the lock screen.

G1.alternative: no: drop s1; s3 then emits transcript entries without touching publish/events_for, per-line cost stays O(history), and D3 adds to it

G2.recommended: persist (append-only JSONL per session, caps as in s3)
G2.alternative: memory-only bounded ring per session (for example 1000 entries / 4 MiB), lost on restart. Simpler, with no file path and no secrets on disk, but the detail view of a resumed session starts empty

G3.recommended: manual, acceptEdits, plan + Default (no flag), gated by probe P1
alternatives: manual and plan only (drop acceptEdits so every write still reaches the inbox)

always pass an explicit mode, defaulting to manual, so a defaultMode in the user settings (such as bypassPermissions) can no longer remove the gate; this changes the current behaviour of existing sessions

G4.alternative: add haiku after a live probe confirms the alias

G5.alternative: bump to schema 2 with a 1->2 load path; a D2 build then shows the unknown-schema banner and saves nothing (a louder downgrade, more code)

G7.alternative: include the first 100 chars of the question or result

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

findings.issue: inbox-updated lets the event copy win outright, unlike mergeInbox's monotonic resolved rule. If an event computed before list_inbox were delivered after its response, an item could regress to unresolved; with per-session deltas it now stays wrong until that session's inbox changes again (before s1 any session's next event healed it). Not reachable today: at load every session is suspended and nothing emits. Cheap hardening: resolved/expired = have || event.

Planned dirty flag dropped. Clean exit is covered (shutdown always snapshots, test shutdown_saves_text_only_changes), but on a crash or kill the text-only fields since the last significant save (last_message, last_activity_at, unknown_count) are lost. Answers, resolutions and status are never lost because they bump inbox_rev or status. Acceptable; the comment there correctly says 'a clean exit never loses it'.

SaveKey must be extended by any later slice that adds persisted state changed on a stdout line without touching status or inbox (e.g. per-line cost/usage), or that state is saved only on crash-free exit. Watch s2/s3/s5 seams.

StartArgs keeps deny_unknown_fields; serde rejects haiku, Opus, bypassPermissions, dontAsk, auto, default, Plan, empty and '--' values. build_args puts --model/--permission-mode after ARGS and before --resume. The only two spawner call sites (start, resume_with; lib.rs passes process::spawn) both pass the stored settings. StoredSession fields are serde(default) Option<String> and re-parsed through the allowlist in restore, so a stored haiku/bypassPermissions loads as None and the session stays listed. Checked claude 2.1.296 --help: manual/acceptEdits/plan and opus/sonnet/fable are valid CLI values. The TS decoder always sets both fields via oneOfOrNull. Every consumer at the tip (SessionList, SessionDetail) is undefined-safe. Re-ran the 5 named tests (1 passed each), cargo test (104 passed, 0 failed), npm test (41 passed), npm run build (ok). capabilities/tauri.conf.json diff 329e93c..4a4a7a9 is empty. Author njcurtis3, no trailer. The P1 probe supports keeping acceptEdits: non-edit Bash still emits can_use_tool. Three notes, no blockers.

findings.title: acceptEdits auto-accepts edit-class shell commands, not just Edit/Write tools
findings.detail: P1 round 2 shows `touch` via Bash ran with no can_use_tool under acceptEdits. Claude's acceptEdits also covers filesystem shell commands such as mkdir/touch/mv/cp/rm in the working dir, which is broader than 'Accept edits' suggests in NewSession. The gate accepted this. Consider a hint on the select label.

findings.title: A non-string stored model/permission_mode still makes the file Unreadable
findings.detail: store.rs types the fields as Option<String>. A file with "model": 3 fails serde and the whole load is LoadError::Unreadable. An unknown *string* loads as None, as G5 requires. A wrong-typed value is a malformed file, the same as any other field, and Rust never writes one. So this is not a regression.

findings.title: TS allowlists must stay in lockstep with the Rust enums
findings.detail: decodeSession throws on a model/permission_mode outside MODELS/PERMISSION_MODES, and decodeSessions maps every entry, so one stray value would fail the whole list. Today Rust can only emit allowlisted values, so it is safe. If a variant is added to one side only, the frontend breaks.

Diff is exactly the 11 approved files; author njcurtis3, no trailer. Re-derived against Rust: Entry (tag kind, snake_case) flattened into Record{seq,at}, Usage, TranscriptPage{entries,next_seq}, TranscriptBatch{session_id,entries}, TranscriptArgs{session_id} all match the TS types/decoders. Rust appends before emitting, and SessionDetail awaits listen before get_transcript, then unions by seq, so no gap/dupe. canPrompt is a Record over all nine statuses (idle/suspended only), notes for the five disabled ones, no box for ended/failed; send goes via answer{kind:reply}, and Rust reply() routes Suspended to resume_with and Idle to reply_line regardless of Finished/Error. costLabel takes the newest turn_result with a cost, never sums. Per-entry decode failures are dropped. Notes: the follow-up draft carries across a session switch (PromptBox not keyed by session id), and a narrow listener window before cleanup. Neither is a blocker.

findings.issue: PromptBox (and SessionDetail) are not keyed by session id; App renders SessionDetail in the same slot for every selection, so React keeps PromptBox's text/busy state across a switch. Type a follow-up in session A, click session B's card: the draft is still in the box under B's header and Send delivers it to B as a reply. Entries are reset on id change but the draft is not. Fix: key={session.id} on SessionDetail in App.tsx (or on PromptBox). Not a blocker because the text is visible and sending needs an explicit click.

The transcript-appended callback does not check `cancelled`. If the selection changes while listen() is still resolving, an event for the old session delivered before the deferred u() runs is merged into the new session's entries (setEntries is shared state). Window is tiny; guard with `if (!cancelled && batch.session_id === id)`.

costLabel trusts that claude's total_cost_usd is cumulative across a --resume (D2 lazy resume spawns a new process). If the CLI resets it per process, the label 'session total' understates after a resume. Matches the plan and the Rust doc comment; flagged for the human-read check only.

The Cargo.lock diff only adds lines (47 new packages). tauri.conf.json and capabilities have no diff since 329e93c. Author and committer are njcurtis3, with no trailer. I worked out decide() against state.rs apply/mark_exit/finish/suspend myself. The inbox only ever grows (push_item is the only mutation, resolve flips a flag), so the len-grew/last() check finds the new item correctly. No path reaches Ended or Suspended with a notice. In on_output, publish_saving drops Inner, then emit_order, before notify runs. The transcript file lock is scoped to append. The per-session gate is never held on the reader thread. Restore never calls apply, and shutdown returns early twice. The focus check uses .ok(), so a missing window or an Err shows the toast without panicking. findings.title: No test proves the notifier runs with no lock held
findings.detail: The rig's recording notifier never calls back into Sessions, so a regression that moved (self.notify)(..) above publish_line would still pass. Reading the code confirms the order today. A notifier that calls r.sessions.list_sessions() in one test would turn that into a deadlock the test catches.

findings.title: A failed toast is dropped without a trace
findings.detail: lib.rs does `let _ = ...show()`. This is best-effort, matches how emit is handled, and the spec does not ask for more. If a toast fails on an installed build, nothing records it.

findings.title: A failed resume is silent, as specified
findings.detail: When a resumed process refuses the id (Result is_error while resuming) or exits nonzero, the session goes to Ended with an Error item. decide() is silent on Ended. That matches the spec's 'never on Ended', but it means a background resume failure gives no toast. Whether that is wanted is a product call.

findings.title: is_focused blocks the reader thread on the main thread
findings.detail: In Tauri 2, is_focused() makes a synchronous round trip to the event loop. Every mutating command is async (off the main thread), the sync commands only take Inner briefly, and the reader holds no lock at this point, so I found no deadlock. After the event loop exits it returns Err, and a toast would still be attempted.

s3.summary: PASS. Re-ran on tip 4a4a7a9: cargo test transcript (12 passed, all 8 named tests present), full cargo test (104 passed, 0 failed, no warnings), npm test (41 passed), npm run build (ok); the state.rs/store.rs grep gate returns 0; author njcurtis3, no trailer; diff is limited to the 5 approved files. I re-derived each property from the code rather than the builder's notes. Snapshot/StoredSession/PersistedSession carry no transcript field. A file name is built only by TranscriptStore::path, gated by is_session_id (s plus digits, at most 20 bytes), and every caller checks the session map first. Caps use truncate_bytes, which backs off to a char boundary. The 16 MiB cap writes one Truncated record, then stops, and that holds across a restart. Image and base64 blocks never leak their data. The two Inner acquisitions in on_output are not a hazard: a shutdown in between yields at most one true line on disk that is not emitted. Recording the prompt after the write is correct. Notes: load() reads only the last line, so a torn tail resets seq to 1; a stale sN.jsonl can be inherited if ids restart; id/name are not capped.

findings.title: A torn last line makes seq restart at 1 and glues the next record onto the fragment
findings.detail:
TranscriptStore::load parses only text.lines().rev().take(1). Take a file whose final line is a partial record without a newline, e.g. ...
{"seq":7,"at":1,"kind":"assis. That can come from a disk-full write_all, a crash, or app exit while a reader thread that passed the live check is mid-append. The parse fails, next_seq stays 1, and the next append writes {"seq":1,...} straight after the fragment. That line is lost, and later records reuse seq 2, 3, ... which are already in the file. detail.ts merges by seq with 'the copy already held wins', so after a reload the new entries are hidden behind the old ones with the same seq. Fix: take the max seq over all parseable lines, and write a leading '
' when the file does not end with one. Not a REJECT, because the trigger is an abnormal write, and session state and state.json are unaffected.

findings.title: Transcript files outlive the id counter: a reused sN inherits an old sN.jsonl
findings.detail: Ids come from next_session in state.json. The transcripts dir is never pruned, and nothing ties it to that counter. If state.json is missing while transcripts/ survives, ids restart at s1 and the new s1 appends to the old s1.jsonl. That happens when a user deletes state.json to reset, or when a crash loses the async snapshot queued by start(). The detail view then opens with another conversation. If that file had reached its cap, the new session also records nothing. The plan's 'exists in the session map' check is satisfied, but it does not prevent this. A cheap guard is to truncate or rotate sN.jsonl when start() allocates a fresh id.

findings.title: ToolUse.id/name and ToolResult.tool_use_id are not capped
findings.detail: Only text, content and input_preview are capped, so an oversized id or name from claude goes into the file and the event as-is. Claude generates these, so the risk is small. A 256-byte cap would complete the bounds.

findings.title: Memory backend keeps up to 16 MiB per session for the whole run
findings.detail: With storage off, FileState.mem is never evicted, so memory is bounded only by 16 MiB times the number of sessions. That is acceptable for a run with storage off, and recorded here for reference.

findings.title: Judged: prompt recorded after a successful write; on_output's double Inner lock
findings.detail: Recording after the write means a prompt that never reached claude is never shown, which is correct. The race this opens is a reader appending claude's reply before the prompt is recorded. Real claude takes far longer than one append to answer, and the frontend sorts by seq, so the worst case is a cosmetic reorder. For on_output: stop() between the live check and apply only marks Stopped, and the line is still recorded truthfully. Shutdown between them means the entry is on disk but not emitted, which get_transcript recovers. No transcript write starts after shutting_down is observed. The transcript mutex and Inner are never nested: append is called with no Inner guard, and read takes Inner only for the contains_key check before taking the file lock.

attempt_2.summary: REJECT. I re-ran cargo test transcript on a533f9f (14 passed, both new tests among them) and the full cargo test (106 passed, 0 failed, no warnings). The diff touches only transcript.rs; the author is njcurtis3 and there is no trailer. The ASCII case is fixed. next_seq is now the max seq plus 1 across all parseable lines, a torn tail gets a newline first (also when that first write is the Truncated marker, which I probed), the byte count includes that newline, and treating any Truncated record as full is sound. Empty and missing files still start at seq 1. The attempt-1 properties are unchanged. The fix is not complete, though. load() still uses fs::read_to_string. A tear inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character makes the whole file invalid UTF-8, so the read fails and load treats the file as missing. I probed this with 7 good lines and then a fragment cut inside the e-acute of café. The next append got seq 1 and was written onto the end of the fragment, and read() returned 0 entries, so every earlier entry went missing from get_transcript. That is the attempt-1 bug again, and worse. Claude's output often contains non-ASCII characters.

findings.title: A tear inside a multi-byte UTF-8 char still restarts seq at 1, still glues onto the fragment, and hides the whole transcript
findings.detail:
transcript.rs load() (and read()) use fs::read_to_string(p).ok(). A torn tail can end at any byte, for example from a disk-full write_all partial write or a crash. When it ends inside a multi-byte character, read_to_string returns Err(InvalidData) and .ok() turns that into 'no file'. So next_seq=1, bytes=0, needs_newline=false and full=false. Probe input: complete_lines(7) followed by '{"seq":8,"at":1,"kind":"user_prompt","text":"caf' plus the first byte only of U+00E9. append("s9", [user_prompt("after")]) returned seq 1 and wrote it straight after the fragment, with no newline. read("s9") returned 0 entries and next_seq 2, because read() also fails on the file and falls back to the empty mem Vec. The 7 good records and all later ones become invisible to get_transcript for good. The byte count also restarts at 0, so the 16 MiB cap is applied from 0 on top of the existing file. Fix: read with fs::read, then String::from_utf8_lossy (or split the bytes on b'
'). Set bytes from the byte length and needs_newline from the last byte != b'
'. Use the same reader in read(). Add a test with a fragment cut inside a multi-byte char.

findings.title: The newline inserted before a torn tail is not counted in the cap check
findings.detail:
The cap check (st.bytes + text.len() + line.len() + 1) runs before the leading '
' is inserted. That byte is added to st.bytes afterwards, so the file can end up 1 byte over max_file_bytes. The Truncated marker already goes past the cap by its own length, so this is harmless. Noted for completeness.

findings.title: A failed write clears needs_newline anyway
findings.detail: If write_all fails (for example the open fails), needs_newline is still set to false and bytes still goes up. Once the disk recovers, the next append can be glued onto the torn tail. This matches the existing policy that a failed write is still counted, so it is a note only.

attempt_3.summary: PASS. On 413f619 I re-ran cargo test transcript (16 passed, all 8 named tests among them) and a full cargo test after a forced rebuild (108 passed, 0 failed, no warnings). The state.rs/store.rs grep gate returns 0. The tree is clean, the diff since 27545c6 touches only transcript.rs, the author is njcurtis3 and there is no trailer. I re-derived the fix from the code. load() and read() share read_raw, which reads bytes with from_utf8_lossy, so an invalid-UTF-8 file no longer reads as missing. bytes is the raw length and torn comes from the last raw byte. The cap check adds the separator newline on every entry of a batch, and that matches the bytes actually written. needs_newline is cleared only when write_all returns Ok. I added temporary probes and then removed them. A 4-byte emoji torn after 2 bytes plus a 0xFF byte inside a complete line: history was kept (seq = max+1). The Truncated marker was written and still held after a restart. A write that failed on a read-only file kept needs_newline, and the next write started on its own line. Notes: any read error is still treated as missing, as in 7c427b9. The Truncated marker can push the file a few dozen bytes past 16 MiB.

findings.issue: read_raw maps every fs::read error to None, as if the file were missing. If a transient read error happens on first touch (on Windows, AV or an indexer holding the file gives a sharing violation, or permission is denied), load() sets loaded=true, next_seq=1, bytes=0, full=false and needs_newline=false for the rest of the process. The next append then repeats seq numbers, can glue onto a torn tail and resets the cap accounting. This is unchanged from 7c427b9 (read_to_string().ok()), so it is not a regression. It is acceptable for the slice because the error is rare and needs an external process. A follow-up could treat only ErrorKind::NotFound as missing and leave loaded=false otherwise.

The Truncated marker is written without checking that it fits. A file within ~50 bytes of the cap can end up a marker's length past 16 MiB. This follows the intent ('past it, one Truncated entry is written'), it is bounded to one short record and was there before this fix, so it is a note only. Every non-marker write, the torn-tail separator newline included, is correctly bounded.

After a failed write, st.bytes still grows by text.len() (and by the leading newline again on retry). The cap side is conservative, not unsafe: the count only ever exceeds the real size. A partial write_all leaves needs_newline set, so the next write starts on a new line. A blank line only appears if the partial write happened to end on a newline, and lines() skips it on parse. Probed: read-only file, then writable again, gives seq continuity and the new record on its own line.

U+FFFD from the lossy decode cannot forge a record. In a torn tail it falls inside an unterminated JSON string, so the line fails to parse. An invalid byte inside a complete line's string value still parses, with U+FFFD in the text. That correctly keeps the record and its seq. No panic path: from_utf8_lossy is total, and parse failures are filtered out.

The attempt-1 properties are unchanged. Neither a533f9f nor 413f619 touches path()/is_session_id, mod.rs, the Snapshot/state/store types or the image/base64 handling, and transcript_text_never_in_snapshot and image_block_is_replaced still pass.
